claims.text: Conventional EAM potentials have limited ability to represent the configurational diversity of ab initio liquids in multicomponent high-entropy alloys near melting.
The proposed reference potential combines a standard EAM potential with a neural-network correction.
The neural network is trained on residuals between EAM and ab initio energies.
The training set contains approximately 10,000 configurations spanning solid and liquid phases.
Learning ab initio residuals will make the hybrid potential-energy surface more representative of the ab initio liquid ensemble.
A reference energy surface closer to the ab initio target surface will improve reference–target phase-space overlap.
Improved reference–target phase-space overlap will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch.
The hybrid reference will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch by approximately 30–40% relative to TOR-TILD's conventional EAM references.
The hybrid reference will yield free energies within ±5 meV/atom of direct ab initio results.
The method applies to multicomponent high-entropy alloys in both solid and liquid regimes.
The applicable temperature range is approximately 0.9–1.1 times the alloy melting temperature.
The expected improvement is limited to high-entropy-alloy compositions within the tested range.
The quantitative performance depends on the quality and diversity of the training configurations.
The predicted 30–40% mismatch reduction and ±5 meV/atom accuracy are based on analogous successes in elemental and binary systems.
Successes observed in elemental and binary systems may not transfer fully to multicomponent high-entropy alloys.
